DRAFT FOR REVIEW

CONFIDENTIAL CASE BRIEF FOR LEGAL REVIEW

From: [SENDER NAME AND ADDRESS]
To: [RECIPIENT NAME AND ADDRESS]

Subject: Sexual assault (criminal)

MATERIAL FACTS

1. Meera Nair, 24, a junior analyst, attended a colleague's farewell party at a rented venue on a Saturday night. She says she drank two glasses of wine and, around 11:30 pm, began feeling unusually dizzy and disoriented. A senior colleague, Rohan Malhotra, 38, offered to put her in a cab. According to Meera, she has only fragmented memories after that. She recalls the car stopping at an apartment building, not her own, and waking the next morning in an unfamiliar bedroom with Rohan beside her, her clothing disarranged, and no memory of consenting to anything. She left immediately and went home.

2. Meera did not report the incident that day. She spoke to a friend on Sunday evening and went to a hospital on Monday afternoon, about 40 hours after the event, after the friend urged her to. She filed a police complaint on Wednesday, five days after the incident, and says the delay was due to shock, fear of losing her job, and uncertainty about whether what she remembered "counted." Rohan admits she came to his apartment and that they had sexual contact, but claims it was fully consensual. He says Meera was "tipsy but talkative," initiated physical contact herself, and sent him a friendly message the next morning. Both work in the same company, and HR has been informed informally.

OUTCOME SOUGHT AND QUESTIONS FOR COUNSEL

[Specify the requested action or relief]

ENCLOSURES

None
